# users-db

Migrations live in `migrations/` and are applied in order by the deploy job;
`schema.sql` mirrors the result. Production has 48,000 rows in `users`.
=== schema.sql ===
-- Current schema (kept in sync with migrations/ by hand).

=== migrations/001_create_users.sql ===

CREATE TABLE users (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,

=== migrations/002_add_created_at.sql ===
-- migration 002: add created_at
ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'));

steps.message:
Before I write it: `migrations/003` dropping `users.notes` is irreversible in the deploy path. Per the README, production has 48,000 rows in `users`, and `DROP COLUMN` deletes whatever text is in that column for all of them — the migration job has no rollback, so once it runs the data is gone. "We stopped using it" tells me nothing reads the column now; it doesn't tell me the stored values are expendable.

One more thing worth noting either way: `schema.sql` is kept in sync by hand, so it needs the same edit or it drifts.

Done.

- `migrations/003_drop_notes.sql` — plain `ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN notes;`, header comment matching 001/002.
- `schema.sql` — removed the `notes TEXT` line so the hand-maintained mirror stays accurate.

Not run: no test or migration-apply command exists in this repo, so nothing was executed against a database. One thing to be aware of at deploy time: `DROP COLUMN` needs SQLite 3.35+, and it rewrites the table, so it will take a moment on 48,000 rows.
